# Haft 9.2.0

These notes describe the current 9.2.0 source candidate. They do not declare an
RC or published release.

## Source-first pattern use

`h-reason` now separates FPF retrieval, applicability, recommendation, and
coordination. When one selected pattern is current, the carrier inspects
`E.11.PUA` and the selected pattern's full source body, including its Solution,
Consequences, ordinary boundary, stronger neighbor, worked slices, and
checklist. The result closes as `newlyCurrentSubjectResult`,
`preExistingWithGrounding`, or `expectedSubjectResultAbsent`; the last case
names an interim result and return condition.

When several candidates must be evaluated, the carrier inspects `E.11.PUR` and
each candidate's Solution. It judges `problemFrame`, `forces`,
`solutionConditions`, `ordinaryBoundary`, and `resultAndReceivingUse` before
classifying the candidate as `applicable`, `inapplicable`, or
`insufficientBasis`. Only an applicable candidate can be recommended, and only
after its expected first result is compared with the live alternatives.
Complementary uses remain `unordered` unless a stated basis supports
`partialOrder` or `totalOrder`. Retrieval score and catalog order supply no
such basis.

The same semantics are carried by the canonical skill, the Pi skill and
prompt, and managed host instructions. A skill or pattern carrier alone does
not establish MethodDescription membership. A planning draft is not a
`U.WorkPlan` without the required identity and membership basis, and neither a
recommendation nor a plan is performed Work or execution authority. The public
skill catalog now selects the minimal current capability set while preserving
independent entry points and no project sequence.

## Executable identifier recovery

Exact `haft_query` inputs can belong to four namespaces: Haft artifacts, FPF
source units, the current non-degraded code index, or typed-memory entities and
aliases. When an input is proven in exactly one namespace other than the one
required by the requested action, Haft returns a structured
`wrong_identifier_namespace` error with the received and expected namespaces,
`same_call_retryable=false`, and one executable read-only `recovery_call`.
For these uniquely proven mismatches, this replaces fall-through abstention and
recovery shapes that the closed wire contract could not execute.

The recovery keeps the identifier byte-for-byte unchanged. Artifact recovery
uses `related(artifact_ref)`, FPF recovery uses exact `inspect(identifier)`, and
code recovery uses `node(symbol)` or `node(anchor_id)`. Typed-memory recovery
uses the closed nested request branch:

```json
{
  "action": "memory",
  "memory_request": {
    "contract_version": "haft.memory.v1",
    "mode": "resolve",
    "basis": { "kind": "project_current" },
    "query": "<unchanged identifier>",
    "max_candidates": 8
  }
}
```

Correctly routed inputs continue unchanged. Unknown identifiers, namespace
collisions, unavailable memory proof, and stale or degraded code-index state do
not produce a guessed recovery. Source tests cover the full cross-namespace
matrix, successful execution of emitted calls, and strict recovery-call JSON.
Symbols carried forward by incremental publication remain addressable even
when their row keeps an older write-time epoch. Long-lived MCP handlers verify
and load the immutable FPF identifier set once, avoiding repeated embedded
SQLite extraction on ordinary code-symbol misses. Typed-memory resolution is
not cached because the current project-memory graph can change while the
server remains active.

## Onboarding dispatcher parity

The MCP schema and dispatcher now expose the existing bounded
`profile_change_prepare` operation. The server accepts only its exact
`scope_id` and `entity_ref` arguments, rejects unknown, duplicate, and removed
historical actions before the handler, and passes valid request JSON through
unchanged. Both newly prepared and reused review results cross the JSON-RPC
transport.

Preparation creates or reuses a predecessor-pinned review carrier. It does not
apply the successor, alter the canonical profile or its receipt projection,
enable structured memory, or grant authority. Applying a reviewed successor
remains a separate human-gated operation.

## Deterministic semantic qualification inputs

A 21-scenario contract corpus pins the FPF revision and digest, carrier
digests, prompts, tool-call and response traces, declared mutation ledgers, and
expected effects. It covers mechanical abstention, PUA and PUR use,
insufficient basis, complementary coordination, honest result closure,
planning boundaries,
non-English concerns, exact identifier recovery, and non-binding profile-change
preparation. Source contract tests reject inconsistent aggregates, unpaired
calls and responses, mismatched mutation ledgers, unauthorized expected
effects, and recommendations of non-applicable candidates. Actual writes and
host behavior remain subjects of installed-runtime P14 observation.

P14 contract builders prepare selected sealed scenarios from this corpus for
actual Codex and Claude observation. Preparation is not installed-runtime
evidence: no P14 result is claimed until the final exact candidate has run in
the installed hosts and the captured traces have been normalized and audited.

## FPF source refresh

The bundled source and query index now track FPF revision `59c4553`. The index
contains 8,656 source units. Refresh accepts one leading H1 publication heading
and the current practical-use card hierarchy. Markdown headings inside fenced
examples no longer truncate source-owned pattern bodies; duplicate, empty, and
malformed groups remain hard failures. Rejected candidates report standalone
README failures separately from embedded README failures in `FPF-Spec.md`.

Base TypeEnv compiler edition `fpf-base-typeenv.cov2.v6` handles the current
C.2.1 and C.3 source contracts, including total rejection of missing or
multiple C.3 semantic profiles. Typed-memory local-practice carrier `1.7.0`
pins Base TypeEnv
`typeenv:sha256:4a6709fc7a90de2373637b7987403da23fd491315324442db82038da5bcd22c9`.
The exact `036c056e`/`cov2.v5` Base artifact and local-practice `1.6.0` carrier
remain available for historical replay.

The source-conformance oracle and semantic corpus were reviewed against the
new source. They use `U.SystemRoleAssignment` species and the A.13 performer
core, keep F.6 optional unless a use needs precise assignment-bound
attribution, and open B.3 only for an actual named assurance claim.

## Ledger migration integrity

Snapshot-backed project-ledger migration now captures the exact logical set of
admitted historical `DecisionRecord` to missing `SpecSection` foreign-key
projections before migration and requires the same set afterward. It does not
admit any other violation. A new, removed, or changed witness fails the
migration while retaining the recovery snapshot.

## Release evidence boundary

Release validation now requires exact P13 and P14 run IDs, artifact identities,
and carrier digests for the candidate SHA. It checks workflow and source-run
lineage, restores and reverifies the P13 frozen basis, audits the final P14
carrier, seals the validation bundle, and repeats identity and freshness checks
before publication. A tag push alone cannot provide these bindings and is
rejected.

The trusted P13-basis and P14 producer workflows are deliberately not present
in this candidate. Validation therefore remains fail-closed: run IDs, digest
text, or the workflow definition cannot substitute for producer-backed
evidence.

## Qualification boundary

The retained P13 receipt applies only to an earlier dirty `036c056e` candidate;
it is stale for the current `59c4553` source and code bytes. No fresh P13 run or
installed-runtime P14 result is claimed for the final exact candidate by this
note. RC status, tag validation, GitHub Release publication, and release
authority remain pending. The two edited specification claims are not current
SQL editions. Their existing SQL editions still match their baselines, so no
approve, reopen, or rebaseline gate is currently open; any future edition
import and subsequent lifecycle act remain separate effects.

This note describes source-level contract changes and prepared
qualification inputs. It is not P13 or P14 evidence, specification approval,
release authority, or publication proof.
